title: Short Stuff: RIP Man of the Hole
summary: Short Stuff recap honoring the Man of the Hole, an uncontacted indigenous man who lived alone for about 26 years in the Tanaru indigenous land in the Brazilian Amazon and who died in August (no signs of struggle, believed natural causes). Covers how FUNAI discovered and tracked him, the holes he dug, his hut and farming, the 2011 footage released in 2018, the decision not to contact him after a visit left him terrified, the likely killing of his tribe by invaders and ranchers, and concerns about Brazil's protections for uncontacted tribes under President Bolsonaro.

segments.title: Intro and overview of the Man of the Hole
segments.summary: Josh introduces the episode as a recap and tribute to the Man of the Hole, who lived alone for 26 years on Tanaru indigenous land and recently died. He notes the man was discovered by FUNAI, dug holes, and that his name was never known.

segments.title: Death, feathers, and the 2018 video
segments.summary: The hosts describe his death in his hammock, reportedly covered in macaw feathers, with no sign of struggle and likely natural causes, and a planned forensic examination. They recall the July 2018 Survival International video, filmed in 2011, showing him chopping a tree.
topics: 2018 video of Man of the Hole

segments.title: Life alone: huts, farming, hunting
segments.summary: Footage and abandoned campsites revealed clues about his life, including 53 thatch huts built over 26 years. He farmed corn, manioc, papaya, and bananas, hunted with a bow and arrow, and used holes with stakes to catch wild boar.

segments.title: Ethics of contact and protection law
segments.summary: After FUNAI visited him with gifts and he reacted with terror and aggression, they decided not to contact him again and only track him from a distance to protect him from disease. Brazil requires sightings to protect uncontacted tribes, and the hosts discuss the moral questions of observing them.

segments.title: Violence against his people and current threats
segments.summary: Local accounts suggest his tribe was poisoned with sugar in the 1970s by ranching interests, and most of the survivors were later killed; he was alone after six others were shot in the early 2000s. The hosts describe threats from drug dealers, poachers, and Bolsonaro-era rollbacks of Indigenous land protections.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts pay tribute to the Man of the Hole, note the preserve's protection may lapse without action, and close the short episode.
